name: Jalapeño Pepper
description: A popular medium-heat chili pepper. Fruits are typically harvested green but will turn red and become slightly sweeter and hotter if left on the plant.
tips: Wear gloves when handling seeds and harvesting to avoid skin irritation. The more you harvest, the more the plant will produce. Flower drop can occur in extreme temperatures (too hot or too cold).
succession: Not typically necessary; plants produce all season long if harvested regularly.
harvestInstructions: Harvest when peppers are 3-4 inches long and a deep, glossy green. They can also be left to ripen to red for more heat. Cut the stem with scissors or pruners to avoid damaging the plant.
containerGardening: Excellent for containers. Use a 3-5 gallon pot with good drainage. Provide a small stake for support when heavily fruited.

soil.notes: Fertilize when first flowers appear, but avoid high-nitrogen fertilizers which can inhibit fruit production.

temperature.notes: A warm-season crop that thrives in heat. Very sensitive to frost.

environmentalAlerts.message: Cover with a blanket or bring potted plants indoors to protect from frost.

storage: Store fresh in the refrigerator's crisper drawer for up to a week. For long-term preservation, jalapeños are excellent for pickling, freezing (diced or whole), or smoking (chipotles).

careTasks.name: Care for Seedlings
careTasks.description: Keep soil consistently moist to aid germination.

careTasks.name: Harden off seedlings
careTasks.description: Gradually expose seedlings to outdoor conditions over 7-10 days before transplanting.

careTasks.name: Harvest peppers
careTasks.description: Harvest when peppers are 3-4 inches long and dark green. Cut the stem with scissors to avoid damaging the plant.

careTasks.name: Watering
careTasks.description: Water consistently, especially during dry periods, to produce healthy fruit. Water at the base of the plant.

name: Habanero Pepper
description: An extremely hot chili pepper with a distinctive fruity, citrus-like flavor. Fruits ripen from green to a brilliant orange or red.
tips: Always wear gloves when handling fruits and seeds. Reduce watering slightly as fruits ripen to concentrate heat and flavor. Provide support for heavily laden branches. Ripening stages are typically green to yellow to orange/red.
succession: Not necessary; plants have a long growing season and produce until frost.
harvestInstructions: Harvest once peppers have reached their mature color (usually orange or red) and are firm. Use pruners or scissors and wear gloves.
containerGardening: Grows well in 5-gallon or larger pots. Requires full sun and consistent watering. Can be brought indoors to overwinter in some climates.

soil.type: Well-drained, fertile soil with good organic matter.
soil.notes: Benefits from regular feeding with balanced fertilizer. Avoid over-fertilizing with nitrogen.

temperature.notes: Requires consistently warm temperatures. Very sensitive to cold and frost.

environmentalAlerts.message: Protect plants immediately - habaneros are extremely frost sensitive.

storage: Store fresh peppers in a paper bag in the refrigerator for up to 2 weeks. They can be frozen whole, dehydrated, or made into hot sauces and salsas for long-term storage.

careTasks.name: Care for Seedlings
careTasks.description: Maintain warm soil temperature (75-85°F) for optimal germination.

careTasks.name: Harden off seedlings
careTasks.description: Gradually acclimate seedlings to outdoor conditions over 10-14 days.

careTasks.name: Support plants
careTasks.description: Install stakes or cages to support heavy fruit production.

careTasks.name: Harvest peppers
careTasks.description: Harvest when peppers change color and feel firm. Use scissors and wear gloves.

careTasks.name: Watering
careTasks.description: Water consistently but avoid waterlogging. Reduce slightly when fruits are ripening.

name: Cayenne Pepper
description: A hot, thin-walled pepper perfect for drying and making cayenne powder. Long, slender peppers ripen from green to a vibrant red.
tips: Excellent for drying - string them up in a 'ristra' or use a dehydrator. Harvest frequently to encourage continued production. The red, ripe stage is best for drying.
succession: Not necessary; plants produce continuously until the first frost.
harvestInstructions: Harvest when peppers are 4-6 inches long and have ripened to a deep red. Cut the stem with scissors. Can be harvested green, but the flavor and heat are best when red.
containerGardening: A good choice for containers. Use at least a 3-gallon pot. The plant's upright habit makes it manageable in smaller spaces.

soil.type: Well-drained, sandy loam with moderate fertility.
soil.notes: Tolerates slightly less fertile soil than other peppers. Avoid excessive nitrogen.

temperature.notes: Warm-season crop. More heat tolerant than sweet peppers once established.

environmentalAlerts.message: Cover plants or harvest remaining peppers before frost arrives.

storage: Fresh peppers keep for about 1 week refrigerated. The best method for long-term storage is drying them completely, after which they can be stored whole or ground into powder indefinitely.

careTasks.name: Care for Seedlings
careTasks.description: Keep seedbed warm and consistently moist during germination.

careTasks.name: Harden off seedlings
careTasks.description: Acclimate seedlings gradually to outdoor conditions over 7-10 days.

careTasks.name: First harvest
careTasks.description: Begin harvesting when peppers are fully red and firm.

careTasks.name: Regular harvest
careTasks.description: Harvest red peppers regularly to encourage continued production.

careTasks.name: Watering
careTasks.description: Water moderately, allowing soil to dry slightly between waterings.
